tutor.text:
Admissibility is a global bound: h(n) must not exceed the optimal remaining path cost h*(n). Consistency is a local constraint: h(n) ≤ c(n,n′) + h(n′) on every edge.

For example, take S → A with cost 1 and A → G with cost 2. Set h(S)=3, h(A)=1 and h(G)=0. All estimates are admissible, but the S → A edge is inconsistent: 3 > 1 + 1.

With h(goal)=0, consistency implies admissibility. Admissibility alone does not guarantee consistency. Try checking both conditions on the fresh graph.
